Preparations were nearly complete. The spectra advanced even faster than Cruxius could have hoped for. After Cruxius gathered ore from the dark planet in the Deep, he had a mission for Vakni. She had been busy with tasks for Valdi and her brother, Ekal, but as she slept one night she awoke into a dream of the Crossroads, just as she remembered them from her last journey here. Cruxius stood before her, his back to her, tossing berries into the air and catching them in his mouth. Vakni gazed nervously into the forest surrounding her. Her last visit to this place was still fresh in her thoughts.

"Lord Cruxius," Vakni bowed. "What can I do for you, Lord?"

"Oh, my dear, please stand," Cruxius chuckled. "I require your worship, but not your degradation. You are a powerful being, in your own right, and I...*admire* you, in a way. It is truly a shame that gods must always interfere with the dance you magnificent creatures perform. But I digress. I have a mission for you, my dear Vakni, and only you possess the skills to fulfill this mission with the discretion I require. Use the skills your old master, Valdi, has taught you, and gather the materials I require. Make the utmost haste. There is little time for leisure. Memorize the list, for I cannot risk letting any know the nature of your mission until it is time. First, you will journey to Ja'Mekan, just past the Southern Forest. There you will steal from the Forge a sample of Geargrite, purified in Roxxarum's eternal flame. From there, you will journey to Fulcrid, where golden spiders spin a silk infused with Fulcrum Threads, which bind the heavens together. You will steal from the spiders, and their queen, a large skein of their silk. Then, you will return here, and take from the Road one of the great paving stones beneath your feet. Once you have these things, you will take them to the Order of Flux in Sentenza, where you will work with the followers there to produce great barrels of aqua animi, which will be modified to meet the specifications of a forgemaster known as Iskandar. You will take with you this..."

With this, Cruxius motioned to the Hecate Road, and a paving stone, glowing golden as the burning sun of Gaea rose from the Road into Cruxius' hand. Cruxius molded the stone in his hands, as if it were no more than a soft clay. He folded in berries and vines from his pocket, and when he was finished, he handed Vakni a [key](http://i.imgur.com/sZ8ontK.jpg) [](#s "like this one, except gold, with primrose vines instead of the green vines here") as golden as the road upon which she stood.

"You hold in your hand the most powerful artifact I have ever personally gifted to a mortal, and I expect it to be treated as such. I shall call it, Sleipnir, and it will neither protect you nor will it strike down your enemies, but carry you swiftly through the world. With this key, I grant you, Vakni, a way to physically transport yourself onto the Hecate Road. Simply imitate the opening of a door as you would with any key, and a portal to my realm will open to you. From the road, you may do the same to return to Gaea. Among the Road you will find thousands of crossroads, with thousands of corresponding signposts. I have printed on them, for use with your key, a map of Gaea, with markings representing the places where ley lines cross. Insert the key into the signpost, and turn, and you will see into the corresponding location in your world. You may step through the portal to journey hence. Use this key to gather the ingredients you need, but be careful, for the thorns upon this key carry the poison you have grown familiar with, and any who grasp it, friend or foe, will require aqua animi, or risk a painful death. Now go, my dear Vakni, and show me what Valdi has taught you..."

Before Vakni could respond, she awoke in her bed. The sickly sweet smell of the Primrose Path lingered in her nostrils, and as she moved to sit up, she felt something dangling from her neck. She reached up and felt the key, hung around her neck by a fine golden thread. She left that night, before the sun rose, being careful to ensure she did not awaken her brother or the other servants of Valdi.
